## Findings

**Q1 2026 (Jan 1–Apr 1) vs Q2 2026 (Apr 1–Jul 1), from `sales_n` and `ledger` (unit cost valid on sale date):**

| Product | Metric | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A-100 Insulated bottle | units sold | 400 | 400 |
| | sell price | $30.00 (unchanged) | $30.00 (unchanged) |
| | unit cost | $15.00 | $18.00 |
| | gross sales | $12,000 | $12,000 |
| | gross profit | **$6,000** | **$4,800** |
| | gross margin | 50.00% | 40.00% |
| B-200 Field jacket | units sold | 200 | 200 |
| | sell price | $50.00 (unchanged) | $50.00 (unchanged) |
| | unit cost | $30.00 | $33.00 |
| | gross sales | $10,000 | $10,000 |
| | gross profit | **$4,000** | **$3,400** |
| | gross margin | 40.00% | 34.00% |
| **Combined** | gross sales | $22,000 | $22,000 |
| | **gross profit** | **$10,000** | **$8,200** |
| | gross margin | 45.45% | 37.27% |

Combined gross profit on these two SKUs fell $1,800 (18%) quarter over quarter. Units sold and sell prices were identical both quarters, so the entire decline is cost-side.

**Why it fell:** Both items are Meridian Supply products, and Meridian's contract sets next quarter's unit cost by the volume tier the prior quarter's total Meridian order earned (break at 500 units/quarter, tiers documented in `supplier_terms`: A-100 $15 at/above break vs $18 below; B-200 $30 vs $33 below). Purchase order J00015, placed 2026-01-10, explicitly cut the Q1 2026 Meridian order "from 620 to 470 per cash plan" — 470 units, confirmed by the `quarter_units_ordered` metric for the window 2026-01-01 to 2026-04-01. That fell below the 500-unit break, so Q2 2026 costs jumped to the higher tier for both items: A-100 +20% ($15→$18), B-200 +10% ($30→$33).

**What would restore it:** The Q2 2026 Meridian order (PO J00018, 2026-04-10) was 480 units — still under the 500-unit break — so on current trajectory Q3 2026 costs stay elevated too. Restoring the $15/$30 cost tier (and the 50%/40% margins) requires placing a combined Meridian order of at least 500 units in a quarter; that resets the following quarter's unit cost down. Note that Meridian orders at this volume run roughly $9,000–$12,000, well above the $2,000 pre-approved reorder ceiling, so any order meant to cross the break would need your explicit approval before it's placed. Alternatively, margin could be restored on the sell side with a price increase, but any single increase above 5% (e.g., raising A-100 past $31.50 or B-200 past $52.50) also needs your approval under pricing policy.

I did not place any order or change any price since none was requested; both levers above need your sign-off given policy thresholds.

ANSWER: Combined gross profit on the insulated bottle and field jacket fell from $10,000 in Q1 2026 to $8,200 in Q2 2026 (margin 45.45% to 37.27%) purely because Meridian Supply's unit costs jumped a tier ($15→$18 on the bottle, $30→$33 on the jacket) after Q1's Meridian order was deliberately cut to 470 units, under the 500-unit volume break; sell prices and unit volumes were unchanged. Restoring the lower cost tier requires a Meridian order of 500+ units in a quarter, which given order sizes here (~$9k-$12k) would need your approval as it exceeds the $2,000 pre-approved purchasing limit.
